clue.text: It helps people to get their bearings

definitions.text: It helps people to get their bearings

parts.words: It helps people to get their bearings
parts.note: bearings here are heraldic devices on a shield, granted by the heralds' office, not compass directions for the lost

explanation.surface: Something like a map or compass that helps travellers find their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearings' suggests navigation, but in heraldry a bearing is a device on a coat of arms; the College of Arms in London grants them.
explanation.definitionFit: The heralds' institution in London grants coats of arms, the heraldic bearings families display.

clue.text: Carrier gets U-boat in an instant to surface

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up to the surface means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a U-boat is a sub, a submarine
a mo is a moment, an instant

explanation.surface: A submarine appears in a flash at the surface beside a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to surface' reverses the whole run SUB + IN + MO, giving OMNIBUS from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus, the full old name being the vehicle, is a passenger carrier.

clue.text: Furnished for the season

definitions.meaning: provided or supplied, as in lending someone help
the forty days before Easter in the Christian year

explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with something is to supply or loan it; also the Christian fasting period before Easter.

clue.text: Ballet girl initially upsets Leslie

indicators.note: initially picks out only the opening letter of the word girl
upsets says the letters of Leslie are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl dancing in a ballet upsets someone called Leslie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ballet' looks like a description of the girl, but it is the definition: the answer is a ballet's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic ballet by Adolphe Adam, first staged in Paris in 1841.

clue.text: New way to carve ham

indicators.note: a new way of arranging the letters of to carve signals an anagram

explanation.surface: A fresh method for slicing a joint of ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the meat to be carved, but it is a verb: to ham is to perform too theatrically.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham actor exaggerates, so to ham means to perform with excessive theatricality.

clue.text: Chief part of a bridge

definitions.meaning: the curved span supporting a bridge

explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix-like adjective it means principal; also the curved span under a viaduct.

clue.text: Master takes female, over fifty, in marriage

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece written over another comes before it

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
Rita is a girl's name standing for any female
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A master marries a woman over fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places MARITA above L in the down entry; 'over fifty' looks like an age.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to wedlock, matters within a wedding union.

clue.text: Where to begin train-spotting, perhaps

parts.note: a station or platform is the place a hobbyist would start watching locomotives, and also generally the place one begins

explanation.surface: Advice on the best place to start the hobby of watching trains.
explanation.definitionFit: The place where something begins, an origin or initial position.

clue.text: He's ragged a lot, may result in disagreement

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words may result in a new arrangement

parts.note: he's is written out as the letters H E S
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Teasing someone constantly may lead to a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ragged' looks like an anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'may result' rearranges all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Two parties who are quarrelling or in dispute are said to be at odds, locked in conflict.

clue.text: A number of workers in possession

parts.note: ten is a number
worker ants are the classic workers in crosswords

explanation.surface: Some employees hold onto a property.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupiers who rent a property are the people holding possession of it.

clue.text: Out of work one may take it

definitions.text: Out of work one may take it

parts.words: Out of work one may take it
parts.note: a passage is lifted from a written work, rather than someone being unemployed

explanation.surface: An unemployed person might accept it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of work' suggests unemployment; it means extracted from a book or other piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract or passage quoted from a longer book or text.

clue.text: A type of wine

definitions.meaning: in printing, a size of type of about five and a half points
short for a port wine of deep red colour

explanation.definitionFit: An old printers' size of lettering; also a deep red style of port.

clue.text: Money advanced for empty apartment

annotationWithheld.why: Money advanced for empty apartment (5): FLAT around O, but 'empty' would have to give O and signal the insertion at once

clue.text: Holy Roman Emperor to turn to

indicators.note: turn says the first word to is read the other way round

parts.note: taken as written, before turning
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to consult a particular emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Several German kings of that name, starting with Otto the Great, ruled as emperor.

clue.text: Quick-it's cold

explanation.definitionFit: Means fast and nimble; also describes chilly weather with a bite.

clue.text: Some cynicism earned a bad mark

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sceptical attitude earned someone a black mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudge or stain, and figuratively a slur on a reputation.

clue.text: Fire confined to part of the church

parts.note: in, as in kept within a place
the spire is the tall pointed tower of a church

explanation.surface: A blaze breaks out only in one area of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' suggests a blaze, but means to stir or rouse someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone with enthusiasm is to stimulate or motivate them.

clue.text: Interval elapsing before giving sentence to a convict

parts.note: time is a prison sentence, as in doing time
lag is British slang for a convict, usually an old lag

explanation.surface: A pause before a judge sentences a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: An old lag is a habitual prisoner in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The delay between a cause and its effect is a period of waiting.

clue.text: An ardent follower of pop music?

definitions.text: An ardent follower of pop music?

parts.words: An ardent follower of pop music?
parts.note: an obsessive fan who trails a band around, the question mark marking a playful description

explanation.surface: Asks who is a devoted fan of chart music.
explanation.definitionFit: A devoted fan who follows rock or pop bands around on tour.

clue.text: Exercise supervision in place of a bishop

parts.note: over can mean in or throughout, as in over the summer
a see is a bishop's diocese or seat

explanation.surface: A bishop's deputy manages things in his absence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in place of' reads as 'instead of', but it splits after 'in'; 'over' meaning 'in' is as in 'over the summer'.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise is to watch over and direct work.

clue.text: Wandering man about desert

indicators.note: about means the man's name goes around the other piece

parts.note: Eric is a man's name
to rat is to desert or betray one's side

explanation.surface: A man roams around a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' is a verb, not sandy land: RAT, to abandon one's side.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means irregular or straying from a steady course.

clue.text: It travels by road and rail

definitions.text: It travels by road and rail

parts.words: It travels by road and rail
parts.note: a vehicle that runs on rails laid in the street, so on both at once

explanation.surface: A vehicle that uses both the road network and railways.
explanation.definitionFit: A streetcar runs on tracks set into the public highway.

clue.text: In a suit designed for a hot country

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters are arranged to a new pattern

explanation.surface: Wearing a suit tailored for a warm climate.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African nation with a hot Mediterranean and Saharan climate.

clue.text: Slash inch off fine fabric

indicators.note: slash suggests cutting the letters up and putting them in a new order

explanation.surface: Cutting an inch from a length of delicate material.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, sheer material made of silk or nylon.

clue.text: Start work in French

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
en is French for in

explanation.surface: Beginning a job in French.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin something, as one would launch an event.

clue.text: The main body, or just the chest?

definitions.meaning: the torso, or the main stem of a tree
a large box for storing or carrying things

explanation.definitionFit: The torso of a body or tree stem; also a large storage box.

clue.text: Foreign country one's entered before

indicators.note: entered says one piece goes into the other

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone has visited an overseas nation previously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's entered' reads as 'one has entered' but means 'one is put inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish name for the Republic of Ireland, abroad from a British view.

clue.text: Punch about the body

definitions.meaning: a strap worn around the waist

explanation.definitionFit: To strike hard; also the strap that goes around the waist.

clue.text: Deliver an item of pottery

definitions.meaning: to deliver the ball in cricket

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the bowler delivers the ball to the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: To send down the ball in cricket; also a round dish.

clue.text: First part of new rise just coming into effect

indicators.note: first part of takes only the opening letter of the word new

parts.note: an ascent is a rise or climb

explanation.surface: The start of a new climb is just under way.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerging or beginning to exist and develop.

clue.text: Showed no respect and ate greedily

explanation.definitionFit: Mocked derisively; also wolfed down food.

clue.text: London slipway used as a market?

definitions.text: London slipway used as a market?

parts.words: London slipway used as a market?
parts.note: slip is a woman's underskirt and way a street, giving a famous East London street market

explanation.surface: A boat ramp in London is used for trading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipway' suggests a ramp for launching boats; split it into slip (an underskirt) and way (a road). Petticoat Lane is a Sunday street market in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-established street market in the East End of the capital.
